headline: Bitcoin is trading around $60,000 on Sunday after bouncing from a two-year low, with money still leaving US bitcoin funds and a busy US data week ahead.

market.asOf: Bitcoin and ether from CoinMarketCap coin pages and solana from Binance.US, read by this desk at about 07:55-08:05 UTC on Sun 22 Nov (15:00 Bangkok). Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 12 out of 100, "Extreme Fear", on the Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index (read at about 08:00 UTC), the same as the day before.

stories.title: Bitcoin slips back under $60,000 after bouncing from a two-year low
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell to its lowest price since September 2024 early on Saturday, bounced back above $60,000, but could not hold that level and was trading just under it on Sunday. It still ended the week about 12% lower, and crypto company shares fell even harder.
points: Bitcoin fell as low as $55,130, its lowest since September 2024, then rose more than 9% to about $60,300, per CoinDesk; CEO Economy, using CoinGecko, put the low at about $55,300.
Bitcoin was at $59,023, up 1.80%, at 07:40 GMT on Sunday after briefly reaching $60,292 on Saturday, per Investing.com.
Bitcoin ended Saturday near $60,121, about 12% below $68,314 a week earlier, per CEO Economy.
Forced selling of crypto bets totalled about $1.8 billion over 24 hours, $1.3 billion of it from bets on higher prices, per CoinDesk citing CoinGlass; CEO Economy said liquidations topped $2 billion.
Over the week Strategy (MSTR) shares fell 30.3% and Coinbase 20.1%, per CEO Economy.

sources.label: CEO Economy: crypto week in review

stories.title: US bitcoin funds lose about $1.25 billion in a week
stories.summary: Money kept flowing out of US spot bitcoin ETFs, the funds that let people buy bitcoin through a normal brokerage account. BlackRock's fund still has not posted its Friday number, and JPMorgan analysts think much of the selling came from everyday investors.
points: Bitcoin ETFs lost $1.25 billion over the week and ether ETFs $221.7 million, per crypto.news using Farside data; CoinDesk put the bitcoin ETF outflows at about $1.1 billion.
On Thursday 19 Nov BlackRock's IBIT lost $541.1 million, its biggest daily outflow since its January 2024 launch, per CEO Economy.
Friday's total was -$124.5 million with IBIT's entry still blank, per crypto.news.
November bitcoin ETF outflows are about $3.59 billion so far, per crypto.news.
JPMorgan analysts put bitcoin's production cost at $86,000 and said retail investors likely drove most of the ETF outflows, per The Block.

stories.title: Inflation data, a Fed hike in view and a big options expiry set up a busy week
stories.summary: Traders widely expect the Fed to raise rates again in December, so this week's US inflation data matters more than usual. US stocks reopen Monday after a sharp tech sell-off, key data lands Wednesday before Thanksgiving, and a large batch of bitcoin options expires Friday.
points: CME FedWatch priced a 95.7% chance of a quarter-point Fed rate hike at the December meeting, per Seoul Economic Daily (19 Nov).
October PCE inflation and Q3 GDP are both due Wed 25 Nov; core PCE is expected at 3.2% a year against 3.1% before, per Newsquawk.
The Nasdaq fell about 10% last week, including 5.3% on Friday, per CEO Economy; CoinDesk put Friday's drop at more than 4%.
Bitcoin options covering 112,323 BTC, about $6.76 billion, expire on Deribit on Fri 27 Nov at 08:00 UTC, per Cryptoticker (data from 21 Nov).

briefs.title: Chainflip hack now put at about $12 million
briefs.summary: The loss from Chainflip's vault includes 122.86 BTC, 520.22 ETH, 3.25 million USDC and 758,141 USDT, up from a first estimate of $4.86 million; the team offers the attacker 10% if 90% is returned by 18:38 UTC on 23 Nov, per Cointelegraph.

briefs.title: BTCS warns its $54 million Aave loan could be liquidated
briefs.summary: The Nasdaq-listed ether treasury company told the SEC its ether-backed Aave loan is at risk; CoinDesk estimates liquidation near $1,450 ETH, and BTCS shares fell 28.1% over the week, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Kalshi faces a Monday court hearing in New York
briefs.summary: A Manhattan state court hears New York Attorney General Letitia James's request for a restraining order on Monday 23 Nov at 11:30am ET; Kalshi's lawyer says it would shut the exchange "for every customer, everywhere", and a federal judge on Friday denied the CFTC's emergency bid to block New York's case, per The Block.

briefs.title: Bitcoin miners squeezed
briefs.summary: Miners' earnings per unit of computing power fell to $26.16 per PH/s per day on Saturday, fees were just 0.64% of block rewards, and mining difficulty is projected to rise nearly 9% around 27 Nov, per Investing.com.

briefs.title: Strategy faces MSCI index removal
briefs.summary: MSCI is due to remove Strategy from its indexes after 30 Nov; its shares ended the week at $77.80, with bitcoin about 20% below its $75,452 average purchase price, per CEO Economy.

briefs.title: Cyber bridge exploit; Upbit and Bithumb freeze CYBER
briefs.summary: About 5.213 million CYBER tokens were unexpectedly minted on Solana in a suspected exploit and sold for about $968,000 in ETH; Upbit and Bithumb froze CYBER deposits and withdrawals, per The Block.

calendar.note: Justice Melissa Crane hears the New York Attorney General's request for a restraining order; Kalshi says it could shut its exchange nationwide, per The Block.

calendar.note: Remarks on the economic outlook and monetary policy, followed by Q&A, per the New York Fed.
October came in at 91.7, per FinanceCalendar.
Both report after the close; Workday's call is at 4:30pm ET (04:30 Bangkok), per Workday.

calendar.event: US PCE inflation (Oct), Q3 GDP (second estimate), durable goods and jobless claims
calendar.note: Core PCE is expected at 3.2% a year (prior 3.1%), per Newsquawk. Q3 GDP is expected at 3.5% against the 3.4% first estimate, per Trading Economics. Weekly jobless claims come out on Wednesday this week because of Thanksgiving, per Newsquawk; the last reading was 203K, per Newsquawk.
The Fed's survey of business conditions around the country, per the Fed's calendar. October new home sales come out earlier the same day at 10:00am ET (22:00 Bangkok), per the Census Bureau.
On Friday 27 Nov US stocks close early at 1:00pm ET (01:00 Sat Bangkok), per NYSE. Crypto trades all day, but thin trading can mean bigger swings.

calendar.event: Monthly bitcoin options expiry on Deribit
calendar.note: About $6.76 billion of bitcoin options (112,323 BTC) expire, with the "max pain" level at $73,000, per Cryptoticker using Deribit data from 21 Nov.
The last jobs report before the Fed decision, per the BLS schedule. November CPI is Thu 10 Dec, the day after the Fed.

calendar.event: Next Fed meeting and rate decision
calendar.note: Two-day meeting 8-9 Dec with new projections, per the Fed. Fed officials stop public comment on policy from Sat 28 Nov, per the Fed's blackout rules. CME FedWatch priced a 95.7% chance of a quarter-point hike, per Seoul Economic Daily (19 Nov).
